question.text: The relationship e^(-rT) × F = S is important because:

answer.text: It shows that Options on Goods and Options on Futures give the same call option price at expiry if other terms and conditions are equal
It proves futures are always overpriced
It applies only to agricultural commodities
It is used to calculate convenience yield

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook, e^(-rT) × F = S links the futures price F and spot price S. As a result, Options on Goods and Options on Futures follow the same pricing principle, and at expiry — if all other terms and conditions are equal — the call option prices on goods and on futures remain the same. The Trap: The identity does not prove futures are overpriced, is not restricted to agricultural commodities, and is not a convenience-yield formula. Note: The equivalence is stated in the workbook for the at-expiry case under equal terms; it is not an unconditional statement that the two option types always price identically.
